chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

When a man supplicates for his brother in his absence, it is called out from the Throne: 'And for you is one hundred thousand times the like of it.' But when he supplicates for himself, there is for him one only. So one hundred thousand guaranteed is better than one of which it is not known whether it will be answered for him or not.

key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne, indicating a lofty divine announcement
key_terms.بِظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ: in his absence, without his knowledge
key_terms.لِأَخِيهِ: for his brother, meaning a fellow believer
key_terms.مِائَةُ أَلْفٍ: one hundred thousand, expressing immense multiplication
key_terms.يُسْتَجَابُ: answered, referring to the acceptance of supplication

ai.seo_question: Why is making du'a for another believer in their absence better than making du'a only for oneself?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the excellence of making du'a for a fellow believer in their absence. It emphasizes that such a supplication brings a vastly multiplied and assured return for the supplicant, unlike a personal supplication whose response is uncertain.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
"When a person prays for their brother in their absence, a caller from the Throne announces, 'For you is one hundred thousand times the like of it.' But when they pray for themselves, they receive only one.
Therefore, one hundred thousand guaranteed is better than one uncertain, as it is not known whether their personal supplication will be answered or not."
